title: Forge 1
description: Implement-from-spec coding tasks graded by hidden JavaScript tests executed in a sandboxed VM (no host access, wall-clock interrupt). Quality dominates the composite 4:1 over performance.

reference.label: synthetic-1
reference.notes: v1 anchors the 1000-point scale to round-number synthetic baselines (0.7 accuracy, 100 tok/s decode) rather than a measured reference rig. A future suite version will re-anchor to measured hardware; per the versioning rules that resets the leaderboard.

tasks.prompt: Write a JavaScript function slugify(s) that converts a string into a URL slug: lowercase everything, replace every maximal run of characters that are not ASCII letters or digits with a single hyphen, and strip leading and trailing hyphens. slugify("Hello World") returns "hello-world". Use standard JavaScript (no imports). Reply with only the code in a fenced code block.

Write a JavaScript function fizzbuzz(n) that returns an array for the integers 1 through n where multiples of 3 become the string "Fizz", multiples of 5 become "Buzz", multiples of both become "FizzBuzz", and every other integer stays a number. fizzbuzz(0) returns an empty array. Use standard JavaScript (no imports). Reply with only the code in a fenced code block.

Write a JavaScript function isBalanced(s) that returns true when the round, square, and curly brackets in s — "()", "[]", "{}" — are correctly matched and properly nested, and false otherwise. All non-bracket characters are ignored, and an empty string is balanced. Use standard JavaScript (no imports). Reply with only the code in a fenced code block.

Write a JavaScript function wordFreq(s) that counts word frequencies in a string and returns a plain object mapping each word to its count. A word is a maximal run of ASCII letters (a-z, A-Z); digits, punctuation, and whitespace all separate words. Counting is case-insensitive and the keys of the returned object are lowercase. An input with no words returns an empty object. Use standard JavaScript (no imports). Reply with only the code in a fenced code block.

Write a JavaScript function fib(n) that returns an array containing the first n Fibonacci numbers, starting from 0 and 1 (so fib(7) returns [0, 1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8]). fib(0) returns an empty array and fib(1) returns [0]. Use standard JavaScript (no imports). Reply with only the code in a fenced code block.

Write a JavaScript function deepGet(obj, path, fallback) that looks up a dot-separated path (like "a.b.c") in a nested object and returns the value found there. If any segment of the path is missing, return fallback instead. Values that are present but falsy (such as 0 or "") must still be returned, not replaced by the fallback. Numeric segments index into arrays (deepGet({xs: [10, 20]}, "xs.1") returns 20). Use standard JavaScript (no imports). Reply with only the code in a fenced code block.
